findings.reason: Correct. Merged with ADV-15. Roth IRA: the applicable dollar amount for a married person filing separately is zero (26 U.S.C. 408A(c)(3)(B)(ii)(III)), so 'Roth IRA eligibility' is in the list. Income-driven loans: under 34 CFR 685.209(e)(1) as in force 2026-11-01 (which covers the new Repayment Assistance Plan as well as IBR/PAYE/REPAYE/ICR), a married borrower filing separately is assessed on own income only, so filing separately can lower the payment; that is stated. The trade-off (separate returns generally lose the EITC and the premium tax credit, 26 U.S.C. 32(d)(1) and 36B(c)(1)(C), with narrow separated-spouse and domestic-abuse exceptions) is stated with 'generally'. P.L. 119-21 was grepped for amendments to 32(d), 36B(c)(1)(C) and 408A(c)(3); none found.

findings.reason: Correct trap, and it bites exactly at this step, when spouses pick plans. 26 U.S.C. 223(c)(1)(A)(ii) bars HSA eligibility while covered by another non-HDHP health plan; Rev. Rul. 2004-45 applies that to a health FSA sponsored by the spouse's employer; Pub. 969 confirms a limited-purpose FSA does not disqualify. The P.L. 119-21 amendments to 223(c)(1) (telehealth, direct primary care) do not touch FSAs. Wording adds the limited-purpose exception so the reader has the fix, not only the trap.

findings.reason: Three parts. (1) 'tend to stall' is an unsourced generalisation: softened to 'can stall' (design rationale, no audit row needed). (2) 'Markdown' is jargon, but the reviewer's 'a shareable file' is inaccurate: the plan view offers 'Copy as Markdown' and 'Print one-pager' (src/ui/app.mjs export row), not a file download, so the text says 'Copy or print the plan'. blocks.body: Your filing status is set by whether you are married on December 31, so a December wedding counts for the whole year. Two incomes withheld as if each were single often under-withhold once combined; run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator together and file new W-4s.
blocks.plain: Whether you count as married for taxes depends on December 31. So a December wedding counts for the whole year. Two paychecks each taxed as if single often don't have enough tax taken out once you're combined. Use the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator together and file new W-4s.

blocks.body: Retirement accounts and life insurance pass by beneficiary form, not by will. In a 401(k), federal law generally makes a spouse the default beneficiary unless they waive in writing; IRAs follow whatever the form says. Read each form rather than assuming.
blocks.plain: Retirement accounts and life insurance go to whoever is named on the beneficiary form, not to whoever is named in a will. In a 401(k), federal law generally makes your spouse the default beneficiary unless they give that up in writing. IRAs go to whoever the form names. Read every form instead of assuming.
